chunks: 1485 - And in al-ʿIlal, which is narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān al-Naysābūrī, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is mentioned that he heard them from al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

That the day of al-Fiṭr was only made the Eid so that it may be a gathering for the Muslims in which they gather and come forth to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and glorify Him for what He has bestowed upon them. Thus it is a day of Eid, a day of gathering, a day of breaking the fast, a day of zakat, a day of desire, and a day of humble supplication. And because it is the first day of the year in which eating and drinking become lawful, since the first of the months of the year according to the people of truth is the month of Ramaḍān, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loved that they should have in that a gathering in which they praise Him and sanctify Him.
And the takbir was only made more numerous in it than in other salat because takbir is but magnification of Allah and glorification for what He guided to and granted well-being.
"And that you may magnify Allah for what He has guided you to, and that you may be grateful."

And twelve takbirs were only made in it because in every two rakʿahs there are twelve takbirs. Seven were made in the first and five in the second, and they were not made equal because the sunnah in the obligatory salat is that it begins with seven takbirs; therefore it was begun here with seven takbirs. And five takbirs were made in the second because the opening prohibition by takbir in the day and night is five takbirs, so that the takbir in the two rakʿahs together may be odd, odd.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: saying Allahu akbar as an act of magnification of Allah
key_terms.تَضَرُّعٍ: humble supplication and beseeching before Allah
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of the Eid prayer
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْفِطْرِ: the day of breaking the fast, designated as Eid

ai.seo_question: Why was Eid al-Fitr made a festival and why does its prayer contain extra takbirs?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the wisdom behind Eid al-Fiṭr as a communal day of worship, gratitude, zakat, and humble turning to Allah. It also explains the increased takbirs in the Eid prayer and connects them to divine guidance, gratitude, and the structure of the prayer.
